REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JULY 10, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.gov in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Verbal comments will be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Mayor/Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Mayor/Chair extends.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. 11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.
12.

Number of Potential Cases: One (1)
Closed Session Report
If the City Council adjourns to Closed Session, the City Council/Successor Agency will reconvene into Open Session after its conclusion and designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.
13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, JULY 10, 2025,
7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Boy Scout Troop 72.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson was noted absent for the record.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to excuse Mayor Pro Tem
  Johnson from the Thursday, July 10, 2025, 7:00 p.m. Regular Meeting
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Johnson (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Royal Plywood Company (Business Spotlight).

  Gloria Perlas Pulido (Recognition of service as Planning Commission Member).

  5B.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to the Cerritos Advisory Boards
  (Boards, Commissions, and Committees) (2025-2027 term) (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, consideration of this item was deferred to the next
  City Council/Successor Agency meeting agenda (scheduled for Monday, July 28, 2025).

  There was no action taken on this item.

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5C.  Review and consideration of the Mayor’s nominations for appointments to internal ad hoc
  working groups and external boards, commissions, and committees (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, consideration of this item was deferred to the next
  City Council/Successor Agency meeting agenda (scheduled for Monday, July 28, 2025).

  There was no action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Richard Vandenberg expressed concern regarding public safety in the City and break-ins
  at Off-Street Café.

  Stephanie Wu expressed concern regarding damage to personal property caused by tree
  roots at her home and homes in her neighborhood, and the City’s claim process.

  Elaine Magee expressed concern regarding pest control and weed abatement on an
  easement owned by Southern California Edison, located near her property.

  Vern Lin expressed concern regarding pest control and weed abatement on an easement
  owned by Southern California Edison, located near her property, and submitted
  documents for the official record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public
  meeting are considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted
  written correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the
  City Clerk.)

  Fernando Sandoval expressed concern regarding damage to personal property caused by
  tree roots at his home and homes in his neighborhood; sidewalk repair; tree root
  removal; and the City’s claim process. He submitted documents for the official record.
  (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are considered public
  record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written correspondence can be
  made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.)

  Sona Bach expressed concern regarding damage to personal property caused by tree
  roots at her home and homes in her neighborhood; sidewalk repair; and the City’s claim
  process.

  Fox Louie expressed concern regarding damage to personal property caused by tree
  roots at his home and homes in his neighborhood, and the City’s claim process.

  Sam Desai expressed concern regarding the City’s business license processing portal and
  requested City Council support of local businesses and attendance at grand openings.

  Maheekanth Murakonda expressed concern regarding public safety, trash, and potential
  selling and use of illegal narcotics near Target on Bloomfield Avenue and Del Amo
  Boulevard; near Tetzlaff Middle School/Claretta Avenue; and submitted documents for
  the official record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are
  considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written
  correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk.)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, July 10, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Samar Malouf expressed concern regarding vehicles speeding through her neighborhood
  and requested additional efforts from the City to mitigate the issue.

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding a recent decrease in home break-ins in the City; Athens
  Services’ cleaning of residential trash bins; requested an update regarding automated
  license plate reader installation; and submitted a document for the official record.
  (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are considered public
  record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written correspondence can be
  made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.)

  Al Barlevy thanked the City for recognizing Jewish American Heritage Month and
  expressed concern regarding recent nationwide and global occurrences.

  David Su spoke regarding support for youth civic engagement.

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency members received
  full-text, unredacted copies of the one (1) written comment submitted for Item 6, by the
  deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies
  of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made during regular business
  hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  The motion carried (4 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Johnson (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

7A.2. Thursday, June 26, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Yokoyama

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated July 10, 2025 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hong, to approve the Register of

  City of Cerritos  July 10, 2025  $10,170,882.17 (COUNCIL)

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending May 31, 2025

  The motion carried (4 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Johnson (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports (continued)

7B.3. Approval of Fiscal Year 2025-26 Budget Amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hong, to authorize administrative-
  initiated Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-26 budget amendments in accordance with Joint Budget
  Resolution No. 2025-19/CSA No. 2025-02 and the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget
  Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project: 110-221-79010 (Land)
  Amount: $375,000
  Justification: A budget amendment is requested in the amount of $375,000 from the
  City's restricted Housing Asset Fund to support the City's purchase of a moderate-
  income senior housing unit located at 19403 Garnet Court, Unit D, within the Emerald
  Villas affordable senior housing community; and

  2. Account/Project: cp23701 (Citywide Facility Network Infrastructure)
  Amount: $243,383
  Justification: A budget amendment is requested in the amount of $243,383 for
  Capital Project cp23701 - Citywide Facility Network Infrastructure. This project was
  originally funded in the FY 2024-25 budget and remains in progress, with work now
  carrying over into the current fiscal year (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Johnson (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Continuance of the existence of a local emergency concerning a gasoline leak from a
  privately owned existing pipeline on the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine public golf course, and
  potential threat to the safety of persons and property requiring remediation, repair, and
  improvement of the public golf course and other City-owned public property, as specified
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hong, to:

  1. Continue the local emergency as proclaimed in Resolution No. 2023-05, at the
  Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course and the nearby City property containing the C-4
  well site;

  2. Make the findings set forth in Sections one (1) through eight (8) of Resolution No.
  2023-05, and incorporate by reference those findings, as they relate to the continued
  existence of a local emergency as specified; and

  3. Direct staff to provide a report to the City Council regarding the local emergency at
  least once every sixty (60) days, pursuant to Section 8630(c) of the California
  Government Code, until the City Council terminates the local emergency (COUNCIL).

(minutes continue on the next page)

  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Johnson (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Approval of annual enterprise and records management support and maintenance
  agreements for Fiscal Year 2025-26 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hong, to:

  1. Approve the annual support and maintenance agreements purchase orders for Fiscal
  Year 2025-26 as follows:

  a. HP, Inc. in the amount of $75,000;
  b. Infor Public Sector, Inc. in the amount of $64,699.94;
  c. Innovative Interfaces, Inc. in the amount of $78,784.16;
  d. Iron Mountain in the amount of $65,000;
  e. JMG Security in the amount of $80,000;
  f. Microsoft in the amount of $108,273.40;
  g. Network Security Operations Center (vendor name changed for cyber security
  protection) in the amount of $54,000;
  h. OCLC in the amount of $52,437.29;
  i. Spatial Solutions & Services in the amount of $50,000; and
  j. Spectrum Enterprise (Charter Communications) in the amount of $159,241.03;
  and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute contract amendments, provided
  that the total cumulative increase does not exceed $50,000 or 15% of the original
  contract value, whichever is greater (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Johnson (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an award of contract to Keen Independent Research to
  conduct an Economic Impact Study of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Paula Eagleman, Theater Administrator. Haley Adams,
  Consultant, Keen Independent Research, provided additional information regarding the
  subject project.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, July 10, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Adrian Ayub spoke in support of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts offering
  nightlife to promote Cerritos as a desirable place for young families to choose as their
  residence and requested the City’s support of the Friends of the 1st Combat Engineer
  Battalion and veterans.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute a professional services contract with Keen
  Independent Research, LLC, in the amount of $75,000, to conduct an Economic
  Impact Study of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts;

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute a budget amendment for a new
  allocation of $75,000 in Fiscal Year 2025-26, with expenses charged to the CCPA
  Endowment Fund; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute contract amendments, provided
  that the total cumulative increase does not exceed 15% of the original contract value
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 1 – 1 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Pulido, Tse, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Hong
  ABSENT:  Johnson (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Directed the City Manager and City Clerk to modify the

  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) (COUNCIL)
